dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: Why did I leave the dojo to become Lord Kujou's instructor...

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: Yanagiha and Okazaki, as well as Mifune... why did they all leave me...

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Toraemon
dialogues.text: ...now, the blade of Iwakura Kouin is the only thing we're missing.

dialogues.speaker: Yanagiha Arashi
dialogues.text: The ancestral "Hakuen Michimitsu Amenoma" of the Iwakura Clan, huh... Say, do you remember, when you and Kunihiko were first adopted, while Master Eiin wasn't looking...

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Toraemon
dialogues.text: We have already been expelled. There's no need to call him "Master."

dialogues.speaker: Yanagiha Arashi
dialogues.text: But Okazaki...

dialogues.speaker: Yanagiha Arashi
dialogues.text: "When you weigh affection against righteousness on a scale, a real swordsman must walk the path of righteousness."

dialogues.speaker: Yanagiha Arashi
dialogues.text: Since Master said so, it means he was not willing to expel us, but had no other choice.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Toraemon
dialogues.text: Of course he was unwilling. But since he has already decided to become the sword of the Shogun and carry out the Vision Hunt Decree, then we can only...

dialogues.speaker: Yanagiha Arashi
dialogues.text: We can only choose our own righteous path. After all, "a real swordsman must walk the path of righteousness."

dialogues.speaker: Yanagiha Arashi
dialogues.text: And yet, Master's own righteousness was defeated in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Toraemon
dialogues.text: That's right. We must avenge them all. Kunihiko, the others — even Iwakura Kouin.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Toraemon
dialogues.text: Such is the righteousness of expelled disciples like ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Yanagiha Arashi
dialogues.text: This must also be Master's blessing. Our first object of vengeance came to us, just like that.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Toraemon
dialogues.text: #You are right. You must be {NICKNAME}. I've heard about your story.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Toraemon
dialogues.text: In the world of swordsmen, only blood can cleanse blood. I assume you are prepared to face the Ex-Iwakura Art Menkyo Kaiden?

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: Why did I leave the dojo to become Lord Kujou's instructor...

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: Yanagiha and Okazaki, as well as Mifune... why did they all leave me...

dialogues.speaker: player
dialogues.text: I've encountered the disciples of the Iwakura Art.

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: Is that so...

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: Are there still people who claim to be from Iwakura? Their Master was such an incompetent soul, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: I am Iwakura Mitsunari. You could consider me a sword instructor here. And who might you be?

dialogues.speaker: player
dialogues.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: Mifune, Tanba... did you see them? The Okazaki brothers, too?

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: Ah, yes, there's also Katayama. He always loved coming up with names for duels before they started.

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: He'd say, "If I become a real master swordsman in the future, then all these duels can written into stories." Hahaha, such nonsense...

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: Right, and we mustn't forget Shimada, who spent the entire "Eiin" and "Kouin" eras training, yet could never advance beyond the rank of Shoden.

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: They fled and became bandits because they could not fathom the power of the Almighty Shogun's Vision Hunt Decree.

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: I miss the good old days of teaching them how to wield a sword. Why in the world did I shut the dojo down and join the army?

dialogues.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, how're their abilities?

choices.text: I'm sorry to say this, but...

response.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
response.text: #Then, {NICKNAME}, who is your master? Is it Domon? Or Shousen? Or perhaps Narukami herself?

response.speaker: player
response.text: I think I might be considered "self-taught."

response.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
response.text: It seems like the Iwakura Art has waned under my watch. None of my students were able to defeat a self-learned swordsman.

response.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
response.text: Whatever your school of swordsmanship is, it doesn't matter.

response.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
response.text: It seems like the Iwakura Art has waned under my watch. None of my students were able to defeat someone who is unwilling to reveal the name of their school.

response.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
response.text: I truly am an incompetent Master of the Iwakura Art. As a swordsman, they call me Iwakura Kouin.

response.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
response.text: Although I have forgotten the key to our secret blade technique and my Vision was surrendered to the Almighty Shogun...

response.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
response.text: ...If you asked me if I still wish to avenge those disciples of mine who could not bear to see my degradation and wound up pursuing the path of wicked ghosts...

response.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
response.text: ...Yet who were incompetent and lost to you, then I do still have some of that fire within me.

response.speaker: Iwakura Mitsunari
response.text: This space is too small. It would be no place for even you to show off your swordsmanship. Come, follow me down.
